questions.question: Define productivity and give three ways in which a business can increase it.
questions.expected_answer: Productivity is output per unit of input (how efficiently inputs are turned into outputs). Ways (any three): train workers; use better tools, machines and technology; improve organisation and management; keep workers healthy and motivated; reliable infrastructure (electricity, water, roads).

questions.question: What is economic growth, how is it measured, and why is it important?
questions.expected_answer: An increase in the total goods and services produced in a country over a period, measured by the change in real GDP. Important because it creates jobs, raises incomes and living standards, and increases tax revenue for services, helping reduce poverty and unemployment.

questions.question: Explain sustainable use of resources, distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources, and give one unsustainable and one sustainable practice.
questions.expected_answer: Using resources to meet present needs without preventing future generations from meeting theirs. Renewable: can be replaced naturally if not overused (water, forests, fish, soil, sun, wind). Non-renewable: fixed amounts, used up (coal, oil, gold). Unsustainable e.g. over-fishing, overgrazing/soil erosion, mine water pollution. Sustainable e.g. drip irrigation, crop rotation, renewable energy, recycling, fishing quotas.
